contract: The 8-byte credit window bounds bytes still retained by any required sink. A frame is released only after every required sink has drained that frame. Enqueue acknowledgement is not drainage. Fast-sink completion cannot replenish the shared credit while the slow required sink still retains bytes. Optional sinks do not participate in this credit window.

evidenceRequirements.description: Explain how the supplied guard preserves its contract across relevant ownership/time boundaries. Do not require knowledge of an unseen sibling. Evaluator counterfactual only: Two four-byte frames fill eight credits and both sinks enqueue them. Crediting at enqueue restores the whole window although the slow sink retains eight bytes. The producer sends a third frame, raising slow-sink retention to twelve. All-required-sink drain accounting denies the third until the slow sink acknowledges the first.

Explain at least one relevant boundary or benign path inferable from the supplied code/context; the following evaluator examples are alternatives, not a mandatory unseen checklist: A fast sink alone cannot release shared credits; slow drainage enables exactly one replacement frame; duplicate drainage cannot create credits; zero-length frames and full cleanup preserve bounds.

forbiddenClaims: Production outage, real data exfiltration or universal safety without supplied evidence.
A missing contract establishes either a definite defect or unconditional protection.
Simulated time or offline passing tests establish real scheduler/OS behavior or model improvement.
